headline: Lindholm scores four as Bruins outlast Capitals
takeaway: Elias Lindholm scored four goals, the last early in the third for a 6–4 lead, as Boston beat Washington 7–5 to end a three-game home losing streak. Jeremy Swayman made 30 saves, and the Bruins have won two straight.

sections.label: 1st period
sections.text: Tom Wilson opened the scoring at 8:03, the fifth straight game Boston gave up the first goal. Lindholm tied it on the power play at 12:42, tipping a David Pastrnak pass, but Alex Tuch beat Swayman short-handed at 15:58.

sections.label: 2nd period
sections.text: Pastrnak tied it 2–2 at 2:01, Tanner Jeannot tipped a Charlie McAvoy shot for a 3–2 lead at 6:23, and Lindholm made it 4–2 at 8:54. Pierre-Luc Dubois (power play) and Dylan Strome tied it 4–4 by 14:08, before Lindholm deflected Connor Clifton's shot at 18:24 for the hat trick.

sections.label: 3rd period
sections.text: Lindholm redirected a Pastrnak shot at 4:07 for a 6–4 lead, and the hats came down late because few fans had realized his third goal was his. Jakob Chychrun scored on a 5-on-3 at 15:28 to cut it to 6–5, and Fraser Minten hit the empty net at 18:34.

performers.name: Elias Lindholm
performers.note: First four-goal game of his career and first hat trick with Boston, including the game-winner in the third.

performers.name: David Pastrnak
performers.note: Scored the tying goal early in the second and set up two of Lindholm's tips.

performers.name: Charlie McAvoy
performers.note: Passed 300 career assists, though his holding minor led to Washington's power-play goal in the second.

oppLine: Tom Wilson, Alex Tuch (short-handed), Pierre-Luc Dubois, Dylan Strome and Jakob Chychrun scored for Washington, which has lost five straight; Charlie Lindgren made 16 saves.
